paragraphs.title: The Siege of Jerusalem and the Removal of the Temple Vessels

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came unto Jerusalem and besieged it.
The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand.
easy.q: Whom did the Lord give into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand?

easy.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar took part of the vessels of the house of God.
easy.q: What was taken from the house of God?

answers: The siege, Jehoiakim’s capture, and the removal of some vessels
The removal of the vessels, the siege, and Jehoiakim’s capture
The building of the temple, the siege, and Jehoiakim’s capture
medium.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar first besieged Jerusalem, then Jehoiakim was given into his hand, and some vessels were taken.
medium.q: What order of events is described in these verses?

answers: Surrounded a city to attack it
medium.explanation: To besiege a city means to surround it in an attack.
medium.q: What does the word “besieged” mean in verse 1?

answers: To the land of Shinar and the house of his god
medium.explanation: He carried the vessels into the land of Shinar, to the house of his god.
medium.q: Where did Nebuchadnezzar carry the vessels?

challenge.explanation: The phrase “part of the vessels” shows that only some of them were taken.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that not all the Temple vessels were taken?

challenge.explanation: The verse says, “And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand.”
challenge.q: According to the verse, who gave Jehoiakim into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand?

answers: The fall of Jerusalem included the transfer of Jehoiakim and some vessels
The siege was meant to teach the youths
The vessels were carried away before the siege began
challenge.explanation: When Jerusalem was conquered, Jehoiakim and some of the Temple vessels came under Babylonian control.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between the siege and the vessels being carried away?

paragraphs.title: The Selection and Training of the Youths at the Royal Court

answers: Ashpenaz, the master of his eunuchs
easy.explanation: The king commanded Ashpenaz to bring certain children of Israel.
easy.q: Whom did the king command to bring certain children?

answers: From the king’s seed and the princes
easy.explanation: The king wanted children of Israel, including those of the king’s seed and the princes.
easy.q: From which families were the youths selected?

easy.explanation: They were to be taught the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans.
easy.q: What language were the youths to learn?

answers: So they could stand in the king’s palace and be taught
So they could work in the fields
So they could lead the army
medium.explanation: They needed ability to stand in the king’s palace and learn the Chaldeans’ learning and language.
medium.q: Why were youths without blemish, well favoured, and wise selected?

medium.explanation: The king appointed that they should be nourished and trained for three years.
medium.q: How long was their training to last?

answers: They would serve before the king after their training
They would all return to Judah
They would stand outside the city
medium.explanation: The purpose of the training was that they might eventually appear before the king.
medium.q: What does “at the end thereof they might stand before the king” mean?

answers: Those without blemish, well favoured, and skilled in wisdom and knowledge
challenge.explanation: The passage describes youths without blemish, attractive, wise, knowledgeable, and able to learn.
challenge.q: Which combination describes the kind of youths the king sought?

answers: They were being trained within the Babylonian court
They were being released from the palace
challenge.explanation: Their new names were given as part of their life and training in the Babylonian royal court.
challenge.q: What may be understood from giving Daniel and his companions Babylonian names?

challenge.explanation: The prince gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar; Hananiah was called Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abed-nego.

paragraphs.title: Daniel’s Commitment to Dietary Purity and the Ten-Day Trial

easy.explanation: Daniel purposed not to defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat or with the wine.
easy.q: What did Daniel determine not to defile himself with?

answers: Pulse to eat and water to drink
easy.explanation: Daniel asked that they be given pulse to eat and water to drink.
easy.q: What did Daniel propose for a ten-day trial?

easy.explanation: Their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than those of the youths who ate the king’s meat.
easy.q: How did the youths look after the ten days?

answers: He feared the king would see them looking worse and punish him
He did not know what water was
He wanted to stop their training
medium.explanation: He feared that the king would see their faces looking worse and hold him responsible.
medium.q: Why was the prince of the eunuchs afraid to agree to Daniel’s request?

medium.explanation: In this context, pulse refers to plant-based food, such as seeds or vegetables.
medium.q: What does “pulse” mean in this passage?

answers: He continued to give them pulse and water
He sent them back to Judah
medium.explanation: After seeing their good appearance, Melzar took away the king’s portion and gave them pulse.
medium.q: What did Melzar do after the trial?

answers: He proposed a short trial so their appearance could be compared
He demanded that the king’s command be canceled
He asked the king to change the food
challenge.explanation: Daniel suggested a ten-day test rather than demanding an immediate change without evidence.
challenge.q: How did Daniel respond to the prince’s fear?

answers: Melzar gave them the king’s meat
Melzar gave them pulse instead of the king’s meat and wine
challenge.explanation: Melzar removed their portion of meat and wine and gave them pulse.
challenge.q: What change followed the results of the ten-day trial?

answers: The request was tested, and the youths appeared healthier
The request was rejected, and the youths became weak
The request was accepted without any trial
challenge.explanation: The request was tested for ten days, after which their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Daniel’s request and the result?

paragraphs.title: The Youths’ Wisdom and Their Appearance Before the King

easy.explanation: The verse says, “As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill.”
easy.q: How many youths received knowledge and skill from God?

answers: He knew how to build the Temple
He was a captain of the army
easy.explanation: Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
easy.q: In what way was Daniel especially gifted?

easy.explanation: The prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
easy.q: Before whom were the youths brought?

medium.explanation: The king questioned them about matters of wisdom and understanding.
medium.q: What did the king examine when he talked with the youths?

medium.explanation: The king found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers in his realm.
medium.q: How did they compare with the magicians and astrologers?

answers: God gave them knowledge and wisdom, and they excelled before the king
God gave them royal clothing only
God prevented them from speaking with the king
medium.explanation: Their knowledge and wisdom came from God and enabled them to excel before the king.
medium.q: What connection is shown between God’s gift and the youths’ success?

answers: Daniel alone understood visions and dreams
Daniel alone was brought before the king
challenge.explanation: All four received knowledge and skill, but Daniel also understood visions and dreams.
challenge.q: What distinguished Daniel from the other three youths?

challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a great superiority in wisdom and understanding.
challenge.q: What does “ten times better” mean in this context?

answers: Training, appearance before the king, and excellence in questioning
Excellence, selection, and return to Jerusalem
Appearance before the king, the siege, and training
challenge.explanation: They were first trained, then brought before the king, where they proved superior in wisdom and understanding.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the youths’ progress?

paragraphs.title: Daniel’s Continued Service in the Royal Court

answers: Until the first year of king Cyrus
Until the end of the three-year training
easy.explanation: The verse says that Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus.
The final verse mentions the first year of king Cyrus.
easy.q: Which king is mentioned in the final verse?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “even unto the first year of king Cyrus.”
easy.q: Which year of Cyrus is mentioned?

answers: He remained beyond the period of training
He left immediately after the ten days
He stayed only one year in Jerusalem
medium.explanation: Daniel continued until the first year of Cyrus, long after the initial training period.
medium.q: What does the final verse teach about the length of Daniel’s service?

medium.explanation: The chapter begins with Nebuchadnezzar and ends by mentioning the first year of Cyrus.
medium.q: Which sequence of rulers appears in the ideas of the chapter?

answers: The first year of Cyrus’s reign
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies the first year of Cyrus as king.
medium.q: What does “the first year of king Cyrus” indicate?

answers: His service continued through a change in royal rule
He stopped learning after ten days
challenge.explanation: The reference to Cyrus shows that Daniel’s service continued beyond the reign and court of Nebuchadnezzar.
challenge.q: What significance does the ending of the chapter have concerning Daniel?

answers: It states the time Daniel continued until but does not describe his activities in that year
It lists all of Daniel’s duties
It says that Daniel returned to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The verse only states that Daniel continued until the first year of Cyrus.
challenge.q: What precise detail can be concluded from the verse without adding information?

answers: It shows that Daniel remained until a later period under Cyrus
It says Daniel served only before Jehoiakim
It describes the beginning of his training
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the first year of Cyrus emphasizes that Daniel remained in service beyond the initial stages of his training.
challenge.q: How does the final verse connect with the idea of continued royal service?
